title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This typed page (numbered 27) has nothing to do with the handwritten motivic and gerbe notes around it, which treat Deuring categories, Picard categories and torsors under H^1(A, F_2). It is a page from a textbook-style typescript on ordinary differential equations, in Bourbaki style, apparently filed among the 'Théorie de Galois des motifs' papers.

Setting: K is R or C, x is in K, y is in K^p, and f = (f_i) is holomorphic (analytic) near (a, b).

Proposition being proved:
- There are neighbourhoods U of a and V of b, and a function u(x, x0, y0) analytic in all variables, such that x -> u(x, x0, y0) is the solution of y' = f(x, y) with u(x0, x0, y0) = y0 (equations (20) and (21)).
- There is a neighbourhood V1 ⊂ V of b such that, for y0 in V1 and x, x0 in U, the equation y0 = u(x0, x, y) has exactly one root y in V, namely y = u(x, x0, y0).
- In modern terms: the two-point flow map φ_{x0→x} is analytic in the initial data, and φ_{x→x0} inverts φ_{x0→x}.

Proof:
1. Substitute t = x - x0 and z = y - y0. This gives a parametrised equation z' = f(x0 + t, y0 + z) with parameters (x0, y0) and initial condition v(0; x0, y0) = 0.
2. 'Th. 2', an earlier existence, uniqueness and analytic-dependence-on-parameters theorem (Cauchy majorant type), then gives the first part.
3. Take M = max ||f|| on U × C, with C a compact neighbourhood in V. The mean value inequality gives ||u(x, x0, y0) - y0|| ≤ M|x - x0|. So for U small and y0 in V1 the trajectory stays in V.
4. Then s -> u(s, x, y) is defined on U. It agrees with u(s, x0, y0) at s = x, so by uniqueness it agrees everywhere. Hence u(x0, x, y) = y0.
5. Conversely, if y0 = u(x0, x, w) with w in V, the same uniqueness argument gives w = u(x, x0, y0) = y.

This is standard local ODE theory: analytic dependence on initial conditions and invertibility of the flow.
errors: Minor implicit hypotheses. U must be connected and convex (e.g. a disc or interval) for the mean value inequality and the uniqueness extension. V1 must be chosen so that its M·diam(U)-neighbourhood lies inside the compact C ⊂ V. These are covered by 'si U a été pris assez petit'. No real error.

ideas.what: Analytic dependence of solutions of y' = f(x, y) on initial conditions (x0, y0), obtained by reduction to a parameter-dependent equation with zero initial value
ideas.modern_name: Cauchy–Lipschitz / Cauchy–Kovalevskaya-type analytic dependence on initial data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cauchy, Poincaré; textbook material (Bourbaki FVR ch. IV, Dieudonné)
ideas.where_published: Standard textbook material; this typescript looks like a Bourbaki-style draft, not a Grothendieck text

ideas.what: Invertibility of the two-point flow: y0 = u(x0, x, y) iff y = u(x, x0, y0), via the a priori bound ||u - y0|| ≤ M|x - x0| and uniqueness
ideas.modern_name: Flow/cocycle property of the solution map of an ODE

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine typescript page on local ODE theory, apparently misfiled among the motivic and gerbe notes. Its content is classical textbook material with no new idea and no connection to the surrounding notes.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription is essentially accurate.
Archival note: the page is a typed fragment (p. 27 of a separate typescript) inserted between handwritten pages on Deuring gerbes. It should not be read as a continuation of those notes.
